div.p: Time-sensitive network (TSN) is regarded as the perspective communication network for the intelligent vehicle application because of its reserved bandwidths, QoS mechanisms, low transmission latency. The message scheduling in the TSN have an important influence on the reliability and safety of vehicles. In this paper, the TSN messages between the vehicular electronic control units are classified into the control data traffic (CDT), the stream reservation (SR) and the best effort (BE). A hierarchical scheduling infrastructure for the three types of messages are presented, which consists of three scheduling strategies, i.e., FIFO, CBS and TAS. For the hierarchical scheduling mechanism, the influences of both FIFO and TAS on CBS are analyzed and an approach for the derivation of worst-case response times of SR message is proposed. The experiments in Vector CANoe show that the proposed method in this paper can effectively obtain the upper bound of SR message transmission in TSN. It can be used to improve the design of TSN system.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: With more and more electronic control systems in the intelligent vehicle, such as advanced driving assistant system (ADAS) and Telematics box(T-BOX), the bandwidth of conventional vehicle networks like CAN, FlexRay is difficult to satisfy actual application demand. As a result, the vehicular ethernet is being applied to the cars due to its high bandwidth and low cost. The IEEE AVB working group, who is charge of the development of vehicular ethernet technology, was formally changed to the time-sensitive network (TSN) working group, which put forward TSN in 2012. It aims at meeting the application requirements of invehicle control systems. The bandwidth of TSN is up to 100 Mbps, and it has strong expansibility and low cost. Therefore, for vehicular networks, TSN has the important research and engineering application value.

At present, there have been a series of studies on the realtime performance of TSN by relevant professional scholars. Yang studied the technical characteristics of TSN in vehicle environment [1]. Liu studied the implementation of multistream attribute registration protocol for the vehicle application [2]. Silviu researched on the relevant scheduling mechanism in the TSN protocol, established a network model and analyzed the influence of the parameters in the scheduling mechanism [3][4]. Kenan compared the performance differences of the normal network message scheduling based on credit value and time-aware integer scheduling under different load conditions in the Ethernet model [5]. In response time analysis, Daniel analyzed the response time of two new scheduling mechanisms in TSN, calculated the upper bound of worst-case response time, and compared the results with those in IEEE802.1Q network [6][7]. The research on parameter design was relatively less. Wang presented TAS mechanism for Ethernet AVB network and the worst-case response time of SR message was analyzed under the TAS [8]. The parameters are designed and the worst-case response time under different values is compared by simulation experiments.

Although the protocols about TSN were studied in the above studies, the message scheduling and its worst-case response time have been rarely concerned. In this paper, a hierarchical scheduling infrastructure for three types of messages is presented, and the scheduling strategies for the different messages are discussed. Considering mutual interference between the messages in the hierarchical scheduling, the time analysis of SR message is conducted, and an approach is presented to derive the worst-case response time of the SR message.

div.head: II. TSN SCHEDULING MODEL
div.p: In the intelligent vehicle, messages in TSN are generally classified into three categories according to different QoS requirements: CDT (control data traffic), SR (stream reservation) and BE (best effort).

The length of the control message byte in the above network message is short, but the real-time and reliability requirements are high, and CDT message transmission can be used. Audio and video streaming message transmission not only requires high bandwidth, but also has certain requirements for real-time transmission. SR type message transmission can be adopted. According to the regenerative priority mechanism in IEEE, a class A message is used to transmit video messages, and a class B message is used to transmit multimedia messages. Other messages in the network that are not required for real-time and reliability use ordinary Ethernet message transmission, corresponding to BE messages in IEEE802.1Q.

All frames in vehicular TSN are transmitted through the switch. In the ports of TSN switch, the messages are queued and scheduled according to some strategies. Different types of messages in TSN need different scheduling strategies to guarantee the quality of service. The optional message scheduling methods for different types of messages are listed in Table I. According to the application requirement of intelligent vehicle network, scheduling method of various messages in vehicular TSN is selected. The messages of the receiving port enter the respective transmission queue after the message is filtered. Since the same queue in the message model has the same priority and does not need to be classified, the FIFO is used for scheduling. CBS which can avoid the congestion caused by message burs is used to schedule SR and BE class messages uniformly. TAS scheduling mechanism is selected according to the comparison of various scheduling mechanisms in reference [6]. To sum up, this paper establishes the hierarchical scheduling mechanism of TSN in vehicle as shown in Fig. 1. The top layer of the hierarchical scheduling mechanism is the FIFO layer, which mainly performs message classification and similar message scheduling, and the port performs frame filtering according to the PCP domain that receives the message. There are four types of messages in the network model, so four queues are set, and each queue has the same priority. FIFO scheduling is relatively simple. The second layer is the CBS layer, which mainly performs SR class and BE message scheduling. The SR class and BE messages entering the layer from the upper layer queue are scheduled according to the CBS mechanism. Class A and Class B messages have their own credit values. The BE message is transmitted in the gap between the A and B credits, which can effectively prevent the message from being occupied by the higher priority message when the message burst is large. The third layer is the TAS layer. The entire communication cycle is divided into CDT time slots and SR time slots. The control message flow in the CDT time slot can be deterministically transmitted through the precise clock. The messages in the SR time slot are based on the link message load and the CBS method. The transmission of SR class and BE messages is performed.

div.p: IV. EXPERIMENT AND ANALYSIS

In order to verify the hierarchical scheduling mechanism and its worst-case response time formula, a simulation model is built in Vector CANoe for testing. Control messages, video messages, and multimedia messages in the network use CDT, the class A messages, and the class B messages respectively. For the convenience of calculation and analysis, the message parameters of similar messages are the same. Referring to the requirements of application in vehicular network [11], the message parameters are configurated with specific values as shown in Table III. The link in ADAS system is selected as the research object and divided into two groups for test: the parameters A a and B a in configuration 1 are selected as reference [10] In order to verify the correctness of the time response formula under the hierarchical scheduling model, experiments are carried out under different configurations. The worst-case response time of Class A (video stream) and Class B (multimedia message) is counted. Comparing the actual worst-case response time with the theoretical response time of different types of messages, the experimental results are shown in Fig. 4 and Fig. 5. It be seen that the theoretical value of the worst-case response time under all configurations is not less than the measured value. The maximum difference occurs when the video message n=2, and the difference is 22 s. At the same time, the minimum difference occurs when the multimedia message n=5, and the difference is 9 s. The worst-case response time obtained by the proposed method in this paper does not exceed the upper bound of the actual worstcase response time, and the difference is small, so the worstcase response time formula and the design of the main dispatcher are reasonable. However the formula and design still have a certain degree of conservatism. Nevertheless, with the increase of network load, conservatism decreases, and the calculated value tends to the true value.

div.head: V. CONCLUSION
div.p: A hierarchical scheduling infrastructure for TSN which consists of three scheduling strategies, i.e., FIFO, CBS and TAS are presented. Under this mechanism, the analysis of worst-case response time for SR Messages is conducted and computing formula is deduced. The theoretical value obtained by this analytical method is very similar to the actual value. It can be used to improve the design and verify TSN System.
